title: Sequences and indexes

sources.locator: CS2023 Software Development Fundamentals; August 2023; section applicable to Sequences and indexes
sources.claim: A sequence stores ordered elements at valid positions; indexed access, update, slicing, and traversal must respect empty input and the first and last valid indexes.

canonicalExplanation.summary: A **sequence** (like a Python list) keeps items in order at numbered positions called **indexes**. Counting starts at **0**, so a list of length 4 has valid indexes 0, 1, 2 and 3 — never 4. Most sequence bugs are off-by-one mistakes at the first or last index, or forgetting the empty list.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
Your to-do app stores four tasks in a list. You want the last one, so you write `tasks[4]` — and get `IndexError`. Why? With zero-based indexing, four items live at valid indexes zero through three. In this lesson you'll trace indexed reads, updates and traversal without off-by-one errors, and a loop condition `index < length` will visit each item exactly once.

```predict
{"question": "`tasks = [\"wash\", \"cook\", \"read\", \"sleep\"]`. What is `tasks[1]`?", "options": ["\"wash\"", "\"cook\""], "answer": 1, "why": "Index 0 is \"wash\", so index 1 is the **second** item, \"cook\"."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Iteration** (loops with a start, check and progress) and **Values and types**. A sequence is one value that holds many values in order.

sections.heading: The mental model: numbered boxes starting at zero
sections.body:
```python
tasks = ["wash", "cook", "read", "sleep"]
#         0        1       2        3
```

| Action | Code | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Read first | `tasks[0]`. | "wash". |
| Read last | `tasks[len(tasks) - 1]` or `tasks[-1]`. | "sleep". |
| Update | `tasks[2] = "nap"`. | third box now "nap". |
| Slice | `tasks[1:3]`. | ["cook", "read"] — stops *before* 3. |

Last valid index = **length − 1**.

```reveal
{"prompt": "What's the last valid index of an empty list `[]`?", "answer": "There isn't one. Length is 0, so *any* index fails. Always handle the empty case before reading `items[0]`."}
```

sections.heading: Walking every item once
sections.body:
```predict
{"question": "Which loop visits all 4 tasks with no error?", "options": ["`for i in range(len(tasks)):`", "`for i in range(1, len(tasks) + 1):`"], "answer": 0, "why": "`range(4)` gives 0, 1, 2, 3 — exactly the valid indexes. The second gives 1..4, skipping \"wash\" and crashing on index 4."}
```

When you don't need the index, just write `for task in tasks:` — Python handles the boundaries for you.

includes: Read, update and slice a sequence using valid indexes.
Trace traversal loops that visit each item exactly once, including an empty list.
excludes: Linked lists and arrays in memory (DSA course).

outcomes: Trace indexed reads, updates and traversal without off-by-one errors.

examples.title: Four items, indexes zero to three
examples.situation: For four items with zero-based indexing, valid indexes are zero through three and a loop condition index less than length visits each exactly once.
walkthrough: **Length:** the list has 4 items, so `len(tasks)` is 4.
**Valid indexes:** zero-based indexing gives 0, 1, 2, 3; index 4 is out of range.
**Loop:** `i = 0; while i < len(tasks)` visits indexes 0 to 3 and stops when i is 4.
examples.result: Each of the four items is visited exactly once, and index four is never read.

examples.title: The last-item bug
examples.situation: `scores = [70, 85, 90]`, and the code does `print(scores[len(scores)])` to show the latest score.
walkthrough: `scores[3]` asks for index 3, past the last valid index of 2, so it is out of range → `IndexError`.
examples.result: The buggy line crashes; the fixed one prints 90.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A sequence of length four has a valid element at index four, because the length names the last position.
misconceptions.correction: Length counts items, but indexes start at 0, so the last valid index is length − 1. For four items, valid indexes are 0 to 3; index 4 is out of range.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The last-item bug", which index does `scores[len(scores)]` ask for, and does it exist?

analogy.example: Like **floors in a building that starts at ground floor 0**: a 4-storey building has floors 0, 1, 2, 3. Pressing "4" in the lift takes you nowhere.
usefulFor: seeing why length − 1 is the top
limitations: Buildings don't grow; lists can have items appended or removed, changing the last index.
Negative indexes like -1 (count from the end) have no building equivalent.

steps.explanation: The loop begins at index zero with a length of four.
At index three the check 3 < 4 passes and the last task prints.
Index four fails the check, so the loop stops without an IndexError.

trace.textAlternative: Traversing four tasks by index. Step 1, Start: len(tasks) is 4; i is 0. The loop begins at index zero with a length of four. Step 2, Last visit: i is 3; printed is sleep. At index three the check 3 < 4 passes and the last task prints. Step 3, Stop: i is 4; i < 4 is False. Index four fails the check, so the loop stops without an IndexError.

faded.prompt: For "Four items, indexes zero to three", explain in three lines the valid indexes for four items, how the loop condition index less than length works, and why nothing is visited twice.
scaffold: Line 3: why each item is visited exactly once.
expectedEvidence: Names the example "Four items, indexes zero to three": four items with zero-based indexing.
Valid indexes are zero through three.
The loop condition index less than length stops when index reaches 4.
Each item is visited exactly once, with no IndexError.

nearTransfer.prompt: For `letters = ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]`, write the index of the first and last item, the result of `letters[1:4]`, and what happens with `letters[5]`.
scaffold: Slices stop before the end number.

farTransfer.prompt: Write a function `middle(items)` that returns the middle element of a list with an odd length, and returns `None` for an empty list. Test it with lengths 0, 1 and 5.
expectedEvidence: Handles empty list, and gives correct results for lengths 1 and 5.

remediation.explanation: Write the list on paper with the index number under each item. Before any `items[k]`, check that k is between 0 and length − 1.
remediation.retryPrompt: Do this for "The last-item bug" and circle the index the code asked for.

recap.summary: To trace indexed reads, updates and traversal, remember indexes run from 0 to length − 1. A loop with `i < len(items)` visits each item once without off-by-one errors, slices stop before their end, and an empty list has no valid index at all.
